chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan al-Jammal, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: 'O Abu Hamzah, ablution before food and after food, the two of them remove poverty.' I said: 'With my father and mother as ransom, they remove.' He said: 'They melt (it away).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and material benefit of performing ablution before and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the spiritual practice of ablution before and after meals to the alleviation of poverty, emphasizing the transformative power of ritual purity in daily sustenance. The Imam’s correction of 'removing' to 'melting' (yudhiban) suggests a gradual dissolving of material lack, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that physical rituals have profound metaphysical effects on one's worldly condition. This highlights the interconnectedness of bodily discipline and economic well-being in Islamic asceticism.
